patients.summary: Construction worker with hypertension, gout and recurrent kidney stones who joined in 2020. Course: right supraspinatus tear (2021, re-injured 2024), allopurinol-induced interstitial nephritis (2021), ureteral stones (2022, 2025), clear cell renal cell carcinoma treated by left partial nephrectomy (2023), and flail chest with hypoxemic respiratory failure after a scaffold fall (2026). Sparse outside records.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller Matthew O'Connell, 44, lives in Westhampton. His old PCP retired over the summer and he wants a doctor he can actually reach. Works construction, early starts, asked for a first visit late morning or early afternoon. Explained the membership and that insurance still covers labs and imaging. Booked new patient visit 9/9 at 1:00. Will sign the release so we can get his old chart. Takes two blood pressure pills, will bring the bottles.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44M here to establish. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

HPI: Blood pressure treated for about six years, currently lisinopril 10 and HCTZ 12.5 once a day, brought both bottles. Rarely checks at home. Gout for a few years, mostly the big toe, last flare was a while back, never been on a preventive medicine for it. Has passed several kidney stones over the years, all on his own, never needed a scope or lithotripsy. Father had stones too. No chest pain, no shortness of breath with work, no headaches.

PMH: hypertension, gout, recurrent nephrolithiasis.
PSH: tonsils out as a kid.
Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, HCTZ 12.5 mg daily, acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for aches.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (does not remember the reaction, was told as a child).
FH: father recurrent kidney stones; mother hypertension; paternal uncle gout.
SH: construction, framing and roofing mostly. Quit cigarettes in 2018, about 15 pack-years. Beer once or twice a week. Single, lives in Westhampton.

Exam: BP and vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing, muscular. HEENT normal, tonsils absent. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness. Extremities without edema, no tophi, toe joints quiet. Skin without rash.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 2.

Assessment/plan:
1. Hypertension, on two agents, reasonable control in clinic today. Continue. CMP.
2. Gout, infrequent flares, no ULT. Discussed, he would rather wait. Revisit if flares pick up.
3. Recurrent nephrolithiasis. Fluids, especially on hot job sites. Call with any flank pain.
4. Health maintenance: CBC, lipids, one-time HCV and HIV screening today. Flu shot next month. Colon cancer screening will come up at 45.
Follow up in 6 months or sooner.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Matthew, your labs from Wednesday look good. Kidney function and potassium are normal on the water pill, blood counts are normal, cholesterol is fine, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Records from prior primary care office received by fax, 38 pages. Med list matches: lisinopril 10 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg. Problem list hypertension, gout, nephrolithiasis. Sulfa allergy listed, reaction not documented. Old BP readings in the 130s/80s on current regimen. Several ED visits for stones over the years, all passed. Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior records. Consistent with his history. Nothing outstanding. Scanned.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine

orders.reason: right shoulder pain and weakness, suspected rotator cuff

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Right shoulder bothering him since around December, gradually worse. No fall or injury he can name. Hurts most at night, wakes him when he rolls onto it, and anything over his head at work. Feels weaker lifting sheathing overhead. Acetaminophen takes the edge off. No neck pain, no numbness down the arm.

Also due for BP check: no side effects from his meds, took them this morning.

Got both Pfizer shots at the pharmacy in April, entered from his card.

Exam: BP per vitals. R shoulder: tender laterally over the greater tuberosity area. Active abduction painful past about 90 degrees. Passive motion full. Neck full range, no radicular signs. Strength otherwise intact distally, sensation intact.

A/P:
1. Right shoulder pain, 5 months, night pain and overhead weakness. Picture fits the rotator cuff. Referred to orthopedics for evaluation and imaging. Acetaminophen as needed; avoiding NSAIDs with his stone history and kidneys in mind. Light duty if he can get it.
2. Hypertension, controlled. Continue lisinopril and HCTZ.

conditions.label: Rotator cuff tear of right shoulder
Chronic right shoulder rotator cuff pathology

documents.title: Orthopedic consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedic surgery, sports and shoulder clinic. Date of service 6/21/2021.

Thank you for referring Mr. O'Connell, 45-year-old right-hand-dominant carpenter.

He describes six months of right shoulder pain with slowly increasing weakness. Night pain disturbs his sleep. Overhead work aggravates it. He recalls no recent trauma.

Meds: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, acetaminophen as needed. Allergies: sulfa.

Exam: Tender over the lateral shoulder. Active abduction is limited by pain and he cannot let the arm down smoothly from overhead; the arm drops partway. Passive range of motion is full in all planes. Neurovascularly intact.

MRI right shoulder (obtained through our office): increased signal within the supraspinatus tendon, consistent with a tear.

Impression: right rotator cuff tear, supraspinatus, on a background of chronic cuff pathology.

Plan: formal physical therapy for cuff strengthening and scapular stabilization, 6 to 8 weeks. Acetaminophen for pain. Modify overhead work. Return if not improving; surgical options would be discussed then.

documents.title: Shoulder
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just an update, the PT is helping. Sleeping through most nights now. Therapist says 3 more weeks. Do I need to come in for my pressure or can it wait till my physical?

documents.title: RE: Shoulder
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. Let's see you in late August, I want to recheck your pressure and talk about the gout too since it's been a while. The front desk will reach out.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP and gout follow-up.

Gout: two flares of the left big toe since spring, one in April and one in July. Each laid him up about a week, he rested it and iced it, did not call. Hard to work on roofs when it flares.
Shoulder: much better with PT, finishing up the home program.
BP: on lisinopril and HCTZ, no issues.

Exam: BP per vitals. Left 1st MTP normal today, no tophi. Heart and lungs normal. R shoulder: abduction now near full with mild discomfort at the end.

A/P:
1. Gout, now two flares in four months. Uric acid and kidney function today. If urate is up he is open to allopurinol now.
2. Hypertension, controlled. Continue.
3. Right rotator cuff tear, improving with PT.

documents.title: Uric acid result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Matthew, your uric acid came back at 8.6, above the goal of 6, and your kidney function is normal at 1.0. As we discussed, I sent allopurinol 100 mg once a day to your pharmacy. Start it this weekend. Rarely it can cause a serious rash or fever; if you get either, stop it and call us right away. We'll recheck the uric acid in about 6 weeks.

documents.body: Got it, picking it up tonight.

medications.reason: suspected allopurinol hypersensitivity with interstitial nephritis

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Seen 9/19/2021. Brief note faxed to PCP.

45M with HTN, gout, chronic R rotator cuff problem. Two weeks of tiredness, low-grade fevers and a spreading red bumpy rash over trunk and limbs. Had a bad sore throat recently and was given an antibiotic at an urgent care. Was started on allopurinol about three weeks ago. Also on HCTZ and lisinopril. Allergic to sulfa.

T 37.8, BP 135/85. Diffuse maculopapular eruption. Joints without swelling or warmth.

Creatinine 2.5 (prior 1.0), BUN 40. UA: WBC casts, no RBCs. Urine eosinophils positive. CRP elevated.

Impression: acute interstitial nephritis, most likely from allopurinol.
Allopurinol discontinued, add to allergy list. IV fluids given. Discharged, needs repeat creatinine with PCP in 2-3 days. Return for worsening rash, mouth sores, decreased urine.

documents.title: ED follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Was in the ED yesterday with a rash and fever, told the gout pill hurt his kidneys and to stop it. He has stopped allopurinol. Rash still there but less itchy. Peeing normally, no mouth sores. ED paperwork not here yet, requested. Booked Wed 9/22 with PCP with labs.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED visit. Seen 9/19 for two weeks of fatigue, low fevers and a rash, creatinine 2.5 with WBC casts and positive urine eosinophils; ED attributed it to allopurinol, which I started 8/27. He stopped it that day. Recent sore throat treated with an antibiotic at an urgent care, he can't recall which one.

Today feels better, no fever since Monday. Rash fading on the chest, still faint on the thighs. Urinating normally. Taking his BP meds.

Exam: afebrile. Faint blanching macular rash thighs, none on palms, mouth clear. No edema. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P:
1. Allopurinol-induced acute interstitial nephritis. Allopurinol listed as an allergy, severe: rash, fever, interstitial nephritis. BMP today. Plenty of water.
2. Gout: no urate-lowering drug for now.
3. HTN: continue current regimen.
Addendum 17:30: creatinine 1.9, coming down. Repeat in 3 weeks.

documents.title: Creatinine recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine 1.2, nearly back to his 1.0 baseline. Messaged pt. Recheck with his physical in November.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 45M.

Interval: AIN from allopurinol in September, creatinine 2.5 to 1.9 to 1.2. Rash long gone. No gout flares since summer. Shoulder much improved after PT, back to full duty, still sore after a long day of overhead work. Booster at the pharmacy 11/3.

Meds: lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: sulfa; allopurinol (rash, fever, interstitial nephritis).
SH: former smoker, quit 2018. Beer on weekends, 1-2. Working full time.

ROS negative except as above.
Exam: well. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign, no CVA tenderness. GU deferred. Skin clear. R shoulder good range, mild painful arc.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P:
1. Interstitial nephritis, resolving; creatinine today.
2. Gout: off ULT, no flares since. Will watch.
3. HTN controlled.
4. R rotator cuff tear, improved with PT.
5. Screening: colonoscopy referral placed, now 45. CMP, CBC, lipids.
Addendum 18:15: creatinine 1.0, back to baseline. Lipids fine.

documents.title: Colonoscopy report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside endoscopy center. Procedure date 1/26/2022.
Indication: first screening colonoscopy, average risk, age 45.
Sedation: propofol, monitored anesthesia care.
Prep: good, adequate for small lesions.
Findings: scope advanced to the cecum with appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Withdrawal 9 minutes. Mucosa normal throughout. No polyps, no diverticula. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.
Impression: normal screening exam.
Recommendation: next colonoscopy in 10 years (2032).
Allergies on file: sulfa, allopurinol.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 8/17/2022, abbreviated note.

46M, known stone former, woke at 4 am with sudden severe left flank pain shooting to the groin, comes in waves, nauseated, urine looked bloody. No trauma, no fever, no urinary infection symptoms. Meds lisinopril, HCTZ. Allergies sulfa, allopurinol.

Afebrile. BP 150/90, HR 98. Writhing. Left CVA tenderness. Abdomen otherwise soft.
UA: RBCs present, no leukocytes or nitrite.
CT abdomen/pelvis without contrast: 5 mm calculus, left distal ureter. No hydronephrosis.

Dx: left ureteral stone.
IV fluids, morphine 4 mg IV, ondansetron 4 mg IV with relief. Good chance of passing on its own. Home with ondansetron ODT, his own acetaminophen, strainer. Follow up with PCP; urology if not passed in 2 weeks or fever.

documents.title: Kidney stone
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Was in the ER Wednesday with another stone. It came out Saturday night, caught it in the strainer. Feel fine now. Do you want it?

documents.title: RE: Kidney stone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news. Hang on to it for now. Keep the water up, especially on the hot days at work. No need to come in unless the pain comes back or you get a fever.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 46M. Sorry about missing the 2nd.

Interval: left ureteral stone in August, 5 mm, passed at home in a few days. No gout flares this year. Shoulder fine most days. Flu and bivalent booster done in October. Colonoscopy normal in January, due 2032.

Meds: lisinopril 10 daily, HCTZ 12.5 daily, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: sulfa; allopurinol.
SH: unchanged. Still no cigarettes since 2018.

Exam: well, tan. HEENT normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no CVA tenderness. Skin no lesions of concern. Joints quiet. R shoulder full range.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
1. HTN, controlled.
2. Recurrent nephrolithiasis: passed stone this summer. Hydration.
3. Gout quiet off therapy.
4. Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Dull ache in the left side of the scrotum for about two months, worse at the end of a work day, sometimes runs up into the left flank. Not like his stones, which are sharp and come in waves. No fever, no burning, no blood in the urine. No injury.

Exam: afebrile. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness. GU exam limited today, he preferred to have urology examine him.

A/P: left scrotal ache radiating to flank, 2 months. With his stone history and the flank component, sending to urology for evaluation. Call sooner for fever or sudden severe pain.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group. Seen 8/10/2023.

Reason for referral: left scrotal pain.

47M, history of kidney stones and a left ureteral stone last year, hypertension, gout, right rotator cuff tear. Three months of a dull, aching pain in the left hemiscrotum that at times travels to the left flank. Denies fever, dysuria, hematuria.
Meds: lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, acetaminophen as needed. Allergies: allopurinol, sulfa.

Vitals within normal limits.
GU: left-sided cord mass above the testis with the feel of a bag of worms, unchanged when he lies supine. Testes normal in size and consistency bilaterally, no hernia. Remainder of GU exam unremarkable. Abdomen normal, no palpable mass.

Labs: Hgb 14.5, WBC 7,000, platelets 250,000, creatinine 1.0. UA normal.

Assessment: left varicocele that does not decompress in the supine position. A varicocele that persists lying down warrants imaging of the left kidney and renal vein.
Plan: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast. Will call with results.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Technique: helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast, portal venous and delayed phases.
Kidneys: 4.6 cm solid, heterogeneously enhancing mass arising from the lower pole of the left kidney, measured in greatest axial dimension, without macroscopic fat. Left renal vein and IVC patent without filling defect. Right kidney normal. No calculi. No hydronephrosis. Ureters normal.
Dilated left pampiniform plexus veins, in keeping with the clinical varicocele.
Adrenals, liver, spleen, pancreas normal. No retroperitoneal or pelvic adenopathy. Bladder normal. No free fluid. Bones without suspicious lesions.
reports.conclusion: 4.6 cm enhancing solid mass of the left kidney lower pole, suspicious for renal cell carcinoma. Renal vein patent. No adenopathy or metastatic disease in the abdomen or pelvis.

reports.text: Staging CT of the chest with IV contrast. Lungs clear. No pulmonary nodules. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. No effusion. Heart normal size.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of thoracic metastatic disease.

documents.title: CT abdomen/pelvis and chest
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Copy of outside CT reports (8/21/2023) faxed to PCP at the request of urology. See structured reports.

documents.title: Urology follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body: Seen 8/30/2023 to review CT. 4.6 cm enhancing lower-pole left renal mass, renal vein patent, no nodes, chest clear. Suspicious for renal cell carcinoma, clinical T1b. Discussed surveillance, ablation, partial and radical nephrectomy. Given his size, location and stone history we recommend robotic left partial nephrectomy to preserve renal function. He agrees. Request preoperative evaluation from PCP. Surgery tentatively 10/4.

documents.title: Patient call re kidney mass
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called him after urology's note came through. He understands it is likely a kidney cancer and that the plan is to remove the part of the kidney with the mass. Anxious but practical, asking about time off work. Answered questions about recovery in general terms; urology will give specifics. Booked pre-op visit 9/20.

reports.text: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No ST or T wave abnormality.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Preoperative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op for robotic left partial nephrectomy 10/4 (urology), for a 4.6 cm left renal mass.

No chest pain, no exertional dyspnea; climbs ladders and carries lumber all day without trouble. No prior anesthesia problems (tonsillectomy as a child). No bleeding history. Not on anticoagulants or aspirin.
Meds: lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, acetaminophen prn. Allergies: sulfa; allopurinol (AIN).

Exam: BP per vitals. Airway normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, normal.
CBC and BMP drawn.

Assessment: low risk for the planned procedure, excellent functional capacity. Hold lisinopril and HCTZ morning of surgery per anesthesia preference; resume after. Avoid NSAIDs and nephrotoxins given AIN history and the partial nephrectomy. Letter to urology.
Addendum 16:45: CBC and BMP normal, creatinine at baseline.

conditions.label: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma of left kidney
conditions.note: pT1b NX, ISUP grade 2, margins negative; left partial nephrectomy 2023-10-04

reports.text:
Specimen: left kidney, lower pole, partial nephrectomy.
Gross: 7.8 cm partial nephrectomy specimen with a 4.6 cm well-circumscribed golden-yellow tumor, inked parenchymal margin.
Microscopic: clear cell renal cell carcinoma. ISUP/WHO nucleolar grade 2. No sarcomatoid or rhabdoid features. No necrosis. Tumor confined to the kidney; no perinephric fat or renal sinus invasion. No lymphovascular invasion. Parenchymal margin negative.
Lymph nodes: none submitted.
reports.conclusion: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma, 4.6 cm, ISUP grade 2, margins negative. pT1b NX.

documents.title: Discharge note
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Brief discharge note, regional hospital urology service.
Admitted 10/4/2023 for robotic left partial nephrectomy, uncomplicated. Ambulating, tolerating diet, pain controlled on acetaminophen, catheter out day 1. Discharged 10/6. Resume home lisinopril and HCTZ. No NSAIDs. Pathology pending at discharge. Follow-up urology clinic in 4 weeks; PCP in 2 weeks.

documents.title: Pathology report received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Surgical pathology report from partial nephrectomy received by fax and filed. Routed to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks after robotic left partial nephrectomy. Pathology: clear cell RCC 4.6 cm, ISUP grade 2, negative margin, pT1b NX. Reviewed with him; urology will set up imaging surveillance.

Sore at the port sites, needing acetaminophen once or twice a day. Eating and moving normally. Scrotal ache a bit less but still there. Out of work until urology clears him.

Exam: afebrile. Port incisions clean and healing, no erythema. Abdomen soft. No edema.

A/P:
1. Clear cell RCC of left kidney, s/p partial nephrectomy. Surveillance per urology.
2. Kidney function after surgery: BMP today.
3. HTN: resumed both meds, BP fine.
Addendum: creatinine 1.1, expected after partial nephrectomy.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu and 2023-24 COVID vaccines given, one each arm. 3 weeks post kidney surgery, feeling well, no fever. No reactions.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual, 47M.

Big year: left renal mass found in the workup of a varicocele, robotic partial nephrectomy 10/4, clear cell RCC pT1b, margins clear. Urology plans CT surveillance, first in spring. Back to work since mid-November.
No stones this year, no gout.

Meds unchanged. Allergies sulfa, allopurinol.

Exam: well. Heart, lungs normal. Abdomen: healed port scars, nontender. No edema. Skin clear.
PHQ-2: 1.

A/P:
1. RCC s/p partial nephrectomy, surveillance per urology.
2. HTN controlled.
3. Nephrolithiasis, gout: quiet.
4. Labs CMP, CBC, lipids. Vaccines up to date this season.
RTC spring.

documents.title: Scan results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI had my first follow up CT for the kidney on the 10th. Urology called, said everything looks clean, no sign of it coming back. Next one in a year or so.

documents.title: RE: Scan results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great news, thanks for letting me know. I'll ask them to send the report.

documents.title: Urology surveillance letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body: Outside urology. Mr. O'Connell had 6-month surveillance imaging after left partial nephrectomy for pT1b clear cell RCC on 4/10/2024: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast and CT chest show postsurgical change at the left lower pole without recurrence, and no metastatic disease. Next imaging in about 18 months, then yearly. Creatinine stable.

Community hospital ED, 8/14/2024. Short note.

48M with chronic right rotator cuff pathology, recurrent stones, history of clear cell RCC. Fell off a ladder two days ago and caught himself on his outstretched right arm, felt a sharp pain in the shoulder right away. Since then cannot lift things above shoulder height.
Meds: lisinopril, HCTZ. Allergies: allopurinol, sulfa.

Right shoulder tender anteriorly. Abduction and external rotation clearly weaker than the left. Passive range preserved. Distal neurovascular exam intact.
XR right shoulder: no fracture or dislocation.

Impression: right shoulder injury, likely rotator cuff re-injury.
Sling for comfort, acetaminophen. Follow up with orthopedics this week or next for MRI.

documents.title: Orthopedic follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedics, shoulder clinic. Visit 9/4/2024.
Known to us from 2021 for a right supraspinatus tear treated with therapy. Now after a ladder fall 8/12 onto the outstretched arm, with pain and overhead weakness.
Exam: anterior shoulder tenderness, weak abduction and external rotation, passive range preserved.
MRI right shoulder 8/30/2024: increased signal within the supraspinatus tendon consistent with a tear.
Plan: physical therapy, light duty with no overhead lifting for 6 weeks, acetaminophen. Recheck if not progressing; surgical repair would be discussed then. Allergies: allopurinol, sulfa.

documents.title: Shoulder
documents.author: patient
documents.body: PT going ok, arm getting stronger. Boss has me on the ground crew for now. Can I get the flu shot when I come in for my physical or should I do it sooner?

documents.title: RE: Shoulder

documents.body: Sooner is better. We have flu and COVID shots on the nurse schedule most mornings. I booked you 10/16 at 7:30.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 48M.

This year: right shoulder re-injured in an August ladder fall, MRI again showed the supraspinatus tear, PT through October, back to regular duty early November with some soreness. Kidney surveillance CT in April clear. No stones, no gout flares.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg, acetaminophen prn. Allergies: sulfa; allopurinol.
SH: construction, quit smoking 2018, 1-2 beers a week.

Exam: well. HEENT normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed port scars. R shoulder: abduction full with a painful arc, strength 4+/5. Skin clear. No edema.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
1. HTN at goal.
2. RCC s/p partial nephrectomy, next CT per urology in fall 2025.
3. R rotator cuff tear, improved after PT.
4. Labs CMP, CBC, lipids. Flu and COVID done. Colonoscopy due 2032. Shingles vaccine at 50.
RTC spring.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 4/7/2025, abbreviated.

48M, recurrent stones, prior left ureteral stone, s/p left partial nephrectomy for RCC. Six hours of severe left flank pain into the groin, nausea and vomiting. No fever or chills. Allergies: allopurinol, sulfa. Meds: lisinopril, HCTZ.

Afebrile, BP 150/90, HR 98. Left CVA tenderness.
UA: hematuria. Creatinine 1.2 (baseline 1.0). WBC 12.0.
CT abdomen/pelvis without contrast: 7 mm stone at the left UVJ with mild hydronephrosis. No signs of infection.

Dx: left UVJ stone.
IV fluids, analgesia and antiemetic in the ED. Home on tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily and ondansetron ODT, acetaminophen. Strain urine. Urology follow-up within 1-2 weeks; return for fever or uncontrolled pain.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED 4/7 for a 7 mm left UVJ stone with mild hydronephrosis, Cr 1.2 there. On tamsulosin since. Hasn't seen it come out yet. Pain now a dull ache, needs acetaminophen at night only. No fever, no vomiting since the first day.

Exam: afebrile, BP per vitals. Mild left CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft.

A/P: left UVJ stone, not yet passed, symptoms improving. Continue tamsulosin. Recheck creatinine today. Urology appointment is 4/23; if not passed by then they will discuss ureteroscopy. Fever, rigors or worsening pain: go back to the ED.
Addendum 16:50: creatinine back to 1.0.

documents.title: Stone
documents.author: patient
documents.body: It passed last night!! Pain is gone. Can I stop the tamsulosin? Should I still go to urology next week?

documents.title: RE: Stone
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great. Yes, you can stop the tamsulosin. Bring the stone to urology; keep that appointment so they can confirm and send it for analysis if they want.

Video from his truck at lunch, identity verified. BP check deferred to home cuff: he bought one after the ED, readings mostly 128-136 over 78-84 in the mornings. No symptoms. Stone passed in April; urology saw him, no further plans other than hydration. Meds lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5.
A/P: HTN controlled on home readings. Continue. In-person physical in the fall with labs.

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 2/12/2026. Copy received with the discharge summary.

49M construction worker, HTN, gout, recurrent kidney stones, chronic R rotator cuff problem (ladder fall 2024). Fell from a second-story scaffold onto his left side. Severe left chest pain, worse breathing in and coughing. No LOC, no headache, no vomiting.

RR 28, tachypneic, distressed. Decreased breath sounds left lower field. Exquisitely tender left chest wall with paradoxical inward motion on inspiration.
ABG: pH 7.45, PaCO2 32, PaO2 60, HCO3 24, sat 90%.
CXR: left ribs 4-7 fractured, each in more than two places.

Impression: flail chest, left. Hypoxemia.
Oxygen, analgesia, trauma surgery consulted. Admitted to ICU.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for severe pain

results.test: Carbon dioxide partial pressure in Arterial blood
Oxygen partial pressure in Arterial blood

reports.text: Portable AP chest in the ICU. Multiple left rib fractures as before. No pneumothorax. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Multiple left rib fractures. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 2/12/2026, discharged 2/20/2026.
Diagnoses: left flail chest (ribs 4-7, segmental); acute hypoxemic respiratory failure.

Course: from the ED to the ICU in moderate respiratory distress, RR 28, SpO2 92% on room air, T 37.2, BP 145/90, HR 110, with a deformed left chest wall moving paradoxically and decreased left breath sounds. ABG on arrival pH 7.35, PaCO2 45, PaO2 60, HCO3 24. Repeat CXR: left rib fractures, no pneumothorax. Thoracic epidural placed for analgesia, high-flow nasal cannula, aggressive incentive spirometry and pulmonary toilet. Did not require intubation. Not a candidate for operative rib fixation per trauma surgery. Weaned to room air and moved to the ward 2/16, epidural out 2/18, pain controlled on oral medicine.

Discharge meds: home lisinopril 10 mg and HCTZ 12.5 mg; acetaminophen as needed; oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed, 5-day supply. Avoid NSAIDs.
Allergies: allopurinol, sulfa.
Follow-up: trauma clinic in 3 weeks with chest x-ray; PCP within 1 week. No work until cleared by trauma clinic.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transitional care call. Home since Friday 2/20 after a scaffold fall with left rib fractures, ICU stay. Breathing OK at rest, short of breath climbing his stairs but better each day. Using the spirometer. Taking oxycodone 2-3 times a day plus acetaminophen. No fever, no cough with sputum. Bowels moving. Discharge papers received today. Booked with PCP 2/25. A friend will drive him.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Fell from a second-story scaffold 2/12. Left flail chest, ribs 4-7 broken in several places each, hypoxemic respiratory failure; ICU with epidural and high-flow oxygen, no intubation, no surgery. Home 2/20.

Now: pain 5/10, worse with coughing and turning in bed. Oxycodone twice a day, acetaminophen. Breathing better, walks around the house fine, winded on stairs. Spirometer reaching about where the hospital wanted. No fever or sputum.

Meds reconciled: lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, acetaminophen prn, oxycodone 5 mg prn (short supply). Allergies sulfa, allopurinol.

Exam: comfortable at rest, SpO2 on room air per vitals. Left chest wall tender with bruising fading, chest wall moves symmetrically now. Lungs clear, no crackles. Heart regular. No calf tenderness.

A/P:
1. Left flail chest, healing. Keep up incentive spirometer, splint with a pillow to cough. Taper oxycodone over the next week; no refill planned. Acetaminophen scheduled while sore. No NSAIDs (kidney history).
2. Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, resolved, on room air.
3. HTN: BP fine, no changes.
4. Off work until trauma clinic clears him; work note given.
Trauma clinic 3/11.

documents.title: Work note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Matthew O'Connell is recovering from injuries sustained 2/12/2026 and is unable to work. His return date will be set by his trauma surgery team.

documents.title: Trauma clinic note
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body: Trauma surgery clinic, seen 3/11/2026. Four weeks after left flail chest. Pain improving, off oxycodone. Lungs clear. CXR today: healing left rib fractures 4-7, no effusion, no pneumothorax. Plan: progressive activity, no lifting over 20 lb for 4 more weeks, then graded return to work. Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Done with the oxycodone, just Tylenol now. Trauma clinic said light duty in May. My employer wants a note from you too saying I can't work until then. Can you send one?

documents.title: RE: Work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Done, the note is attached in your portal letters. Keep walking every day. Let us know if the breathing gets worse instead of better.

documents.title: Back to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Back on light duty as of Monday. Ribs only sore at the end of the day. Staying off ladders for now, believe me. Do I need to see you before my physical?

documents.title: RE: Back to work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good to hear. No, unless something changes. Let's do your physical in early summer; you turn 50 this month so we'll start the shingles shots.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill lisinopril 10 mg, HCTZ 12.5 mg. Last labs 11/2025 normal. Physical booked 7/10. Sent 90 days.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 50M.

Interval: February scaffold fall with left flail chest and hypoxemic respiratory failure, ICU, no intubation. Off opioids since March. Back on light duty since early May, now doing most of his old job except high work. Ribs ache after long days, breathing normal, no cough. Shoulder about the same. No stones since April 2025, no gout flares. Kidney surveillance CT due this fall with urology.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, HCTZ 12.5 mg daily, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: sulfa; allopurinol (AIN).
SH: quit smoking 2018, 15 pack-years. 1-2 drinks weekly. Construction.

ROS otherwise negative.
Exam: well. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally, good air movement. Chest wall: mild tenderness left lateral ribs, no deformity. Abdomen soft, healed port scars. R shoulder mild painful arc, strength good. No edema. Skin clear.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P:
1. HTN, controlled. Continue.
2. Left flail chest, healed clinically; respiratory failure resolved.
3. Clear cell RCC s/p partial nephrectomy, surveillance through urology.
4. Recurrent nephrolithiasis, gout: quiet.
5. R rotator cuff tear, chronic, functional.
6. Prevention: Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months. Colonoscopy due 2032. CMP, CBC, lipids.
RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Matthew, your labs from Friday are normal: kidney function steady, blood count and cholesterol fine. Nothing to change.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Arm was sore from the shingles shot for 2 days, figured that's normal.

documents.body: When should I get the second shingles shot? Fall works better for me, work is crazy right now.

documents.title: RE: Shingles shot
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Anytime from September through early January is fine. Call or message when you know your schedule and we'll put you on the nurse schedule, and we can do your flu shot the same morning.
